result.title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping
result.summary: Large language models serve applications with diverse inference budgets, but training and maintaining separate models for each budget incurs substantial costs. Recent Looped Transformers enable flexible inference computation through parameter reuse, but maintaining strong performance across different inference budgets remains an open challenge. We introduce Accordion, a mixture-of-experts-based model that supports five inference budgets through fixed-prefix layer looping. Each budget follows a pre-defined execution path, while the minimum budget retains the unlooped model. Joint pretraining samples one budget per micro-batch and optimizes its next-token prediction loss without additional cross-budget consistency objectives. We further preserve these inference budgets through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, where parameter-group merging and budget-matched multi-teacher on-policy distillation integrate three domain experts into one model. After 3.6T tokens of pretraining, increasing inference depth improves Accordion-6B-A0.5B's five-category macro-average across 37 tasks by 3.01 percentage points, with the middle budget capturing 89% of this gain using half as many additional layer executions. The final model surpasses each domain expert on its corresponding task-and-budget average, while achieving strong instruction-following performance across all budgets and retaining depth-dependent gains in mathematical reasoning and code generation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Accordion：基于 MoE 的模型通过固定前缀层循环实现五档推理深度预算，最浅档即未循环模型；预训练按 micro-batch 采样单一预算做下一词预测，并用参数组合并与预算匹配的多教师 on-policy 蒸馏在 SFT、RL 后保留各档能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「循环层即额外计算、按预算选择执行路径」及跨预算蒸馏的设定，可能为 LVR 中动态计算、停止/深度决策与 latent 状态训练的监督分配提供核查线索；但工作纯文本、不涉及视觉证据筛选，且未验证 latent 内容是否被实际使用。
